newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - Wisneski strikes twice for Canterbury.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - Wisneski strikes twice for Canterbury.

text.p: Canterbury medium pacer Warren Wisneski rocked Wellington with two wickets in his first two overs in the Shell Cup limited-overs cricket final on Tuesday.
After Wellington captain Roger Twose won the toss and elected to bat in cool, overcast conditions, Wisneski wasted little time making in-roads with some aggressive swing and seam bowling.
He opened with two wides in his first three balls before delivering a third, wider, ball to opener Phil Chandler, who was unable to resist the temptation of fishing for it.
Chandler only succeeded in catching an edge and was taken at second slip by Stephen Fleming for a duck.
Scott Weenink suffered a similar fate in the third over of the morning, but touched the ball directly behind to wicketkeeper Lee Germon.
Jason Wells struggled to get going but had survived until Wellington were forced to leave the field 15 overs into the game at 2-46 as light drizzle turned to steady rain.
Wells was 13 not out while a more belligerent Twose was unbeaten on 22.
Wisneski finished his spell of six overs with 2-17, including five wides.
